notes: Screening results for the first candidate binary only; V2 memory-reuse changes require new measurements.
Every process has one warmup and three measured verified trials; use each process median as one observation.
Main effects average matched on/off comparisons over the other two flags; twelve pairs are clustered in three input-seed blocks, not twelve independent samples.
Construction/evaluation flag effects include their existing parallel dispatch; this does not isolate factoring or batching from parallel scheduling.
Bit-protocol input roots and complete proof contents match baseline across all flags and worker counts; word proofs intentionally use a distinct protocol.
The word binder increases arithmetic eight-worker process RSS by about 13.75% relative to baseline, despite improving latency.
Candidate arithmetic commit time regresses consistently, most visibly about eight milliseconds at one worker; unchanged source bodies do not establish a cause.
Selected policies require fresh holdout inputs after the V2 memory change; no screening winner is qualified by this analysis alone.
